newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan delays stocks warrants debut due tax - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan delays stocks warrants debut due tax - paper.

text.p: Securities regulators will delay debut of Taiwan stock warrants to resolve confusion about related tax issues, the local Economic Daily News said on Tuesday.
The newspaper quoted the Securities and Futures Commission chairman Lu Daung-yen as saying the tax rate on the trading of stocks warrants must be decided before they can be traded.
The latest proposal is to tax warrant trades at between 0.1 percent and 0.3 percent, the paper said.
Officials were unavailable for immediate comment.
In a long-expected June 2 decree that took effect on June securities brokerages with T$3 billion or more in registered capital could issue warrants on qualified shares.
As of late on Monday, 18 institutions had applied to be among the first to list warrants, which have never been allowed in Taiwan despite the relative maturity and big turnover in its stock market.
Six institutions have won commission approval to issue, but still must await resolution of the tax issue.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange is managing warrant issuance under the commission's guidance and will list the instruments.
The exchange has approved 31 stock listings as qualified for inclusion in the island's debut warrants.

To qualify, a listed firm's Taiwan shares must have a total market value, based on June 30 closing prices, of more than T$25 billion, with at least 20 percent of their shares circulating in the market between January 31 to May 31, officials said.
Listed firms also must have more than 15,000 shareholders -- at least 7,000 of whom hold 1,000 to 50,000 shares. (US$=T$27.9)
